episode.title: Losing ground: Somalia and Mali's jihad problem

persons.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
persons.role: President of Somalia's federal government in Mogadishu; remaining in power past his term limit, prompting US frustration

persons.name: Maalim Ibrahim
persons.role: Reported co-founder of al-Shabaab; member of its executive shura; operational and taxation roles; described by Somali defense minister as its ninth most senior member; Somalia claims he was killed (unconfirmed by al-Shabaab)

mentions.quote: this guy named Maalim Ibrahim, who was reported co-founder of al-Shabaab... the ninth most senior member of al-Shabaab... on the main Shura council or executive council

persons.name: Ahmed Moalim Fiqi

persons.name: Abu Bakr al-Mainuki
persons.role: Islamic State West Africa Province leader touted as number two of the global Islamic State and head of its general directorate of provinces; killed in US airstrikes in Nigeria
persons.status_detail: killed in US airstrikes in northeast Nigeria (2026)

mentions.quote: they killed, I believe his name's Abu Bakr al-Mainuki, who was sort of touted as the number two of global Islamic state and the head of their general director of provinces

key_claims: US withdrawal of support for the UN logistics mission risks collapsing the AU mission in Somalia and producing 'another Afghanistan' with al-Shabaab, which controls 35+% of the country, as the next Islamic Emirate.
Al-Shabaab is the most sophisticated operator in al-Qaeda's network and has internalized the Taliban's lessons.
US strikes in Mali without a ground force or political strategy would be 'flashy' but ineffective; JNIM has tens of thousands of fighters and a deep bench.

Visibility into al-Qaeda, especially in Afghanistan, is at an all-time low - possibly by design - so confident claims that it is either defunct or stronger than ever are unknowable; the branches (al-Shabaab, AQAP, JNIM, AQIS) are all strong and none has broken bayah since Zawahiri's death.
AQIS is helping the Pakistani Taliban's campaign in Pakistan and is part of al-Qaeda's core, not separate from it; al-Qaeda describes branches as 'theaters' (al-Qaeda in East Africa, etc.).
Al-Qaeda is rebuilding in Afghanistan with UN-confirmed training camps; the Taliban are stronger than before 9/11 with captured US equipment.
Saif al-Adel is the reported al-Qaeda leader, based in Iran or Afghanistan.
